title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
abstract: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.

bite.hook: Anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing.
tldr: Showed that anti-unitary periodic drives help stabilize Discrete Time-Crystals.
Used Dynamical Freezing where magnetization acts as an emergent conserved operator.
Proved through infinite-chain simulations that generic states show no detectable decay.
bite.whyItMatters: Finding new ways to stabilize nonequilibrium quantum states is critical for developing advanced quantum technologies and memory storage.
bite.eli5: It is like discovering a secret recipe to keep a spinning top moving forever without slowing down, even when nudged.
